name: Low-temperature demagnetization (10 min liquid-nitrogen soak, zero field) of one-inch lava cores in Tsunakawa-Shaw paleointensity experiments
plain_name: Dunk lava rock cores in liquid nitrogen to strip weak magnetism before measuring ancient field strength
description: Before each stepwise AF demagnetization of NRM, ARM and laboratory TRM, one-inch Hawaiian lava specimens are soaked in liquid nitrogen for 10 min and warmed at room temperature for 30 min in zero field (low-temperature demagnetization, LTD), removing multidomain magnetite remanence; remanence is measured with DSPIN/ASPIN spinner magnetometers with AF to 180 mT.
keywords: Dunk lava rock cores in liquid nitrogen to strip weak magnetism before measuring ancient field strength

sources.citation: Yamamoto and Yamaoka (2018) Paleointensity Study on the Holocene Surface Lavas on the Island of Hawaii Using the Tsunakawa-Shaw Method, Frontiers in Earth Science 6:48

reported_equipment: DSPIN automated spinner magnetometer with AF demagnetizer (Natsuhara Giken)

requirements.rationale: LTD is done by soaking the specimen in liquid nitrogen.
Specimens are cut from standard one-inch paleomagnetic cores.
The cooling/warming cycle must happen in zero field so no new remanence is acquired.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
